name: circle the real word in a list of every variant
one_line: One word, one mechanical change applied in every possible way, the whole list printed, and the question is which entries are real words.
how: Take a word of eight letters and print every string got by taking one letter out. There are eight and they sit on two lines. Print how many are real words — on PORZIONE it is one, POZIONE — and settle that count yourself against a word list, because nothing after you will catch it. Removal is fixed here because its list is the length of the word and needs no other restriction: adding a letter to the same word gives 181 rows and will not fit. Then a second half with no list at all: start from a long word and take one letter away at a time, each step a word, three steps of blanks.

knobs.effect: Removing gives as many rows as the word has letters. Adding gives 181 on eight letters. Substituting freely gives 100 on five, restricted to the vowels 8. Moving one named letter gives 6, any letter 30. The antipode gives 2 at any length.

knobs.knob: whether the count of real words is printed
knobs.effect: «One of these eight is a word» bounds the answer, and somebody who circles two knows they are wrong before anybody tells them. Left out, the sheet comes back unmarkable by anyone, including whoever wrote it.
«A letter at the front» leaves 21 tries against 121 for a free insertion, one in 5.8. Declaring where costs one word in the title and is what brings a list back onto a page.
Asking for a chain the sheet cannot print turns the exercise round: the person composes instead of choosing, and the checking leaves the page for a dictionary or for somebody.

where_the_work_is: In choosing the word, not the operation. A word whose deletions give exactly one real word makes the sheet; one that gives none or three makes it unanswerable, and only trying all of them by hand says which.
breaks: It is ink and it prints. Scanned back, a circled string reads only if the rows are set well apart. On 800x480 eight rows of eight letters fit and twenty-one do not, which is why the fixed operation is the one with the shortest list. Composing is where it fails: the eight strings have to be written out by hand and the count of real words checked against a word list, because a model asked for them returns strings that are not deletions of the word at all.
